title: Voice Profile
description: Documents the shape of a voice profile.json consumed by scripts/voice_profile.py. This schema is documentation only and is not enforced at runtime; runtime validation is performed by validate_profile() in scripts/voice_profile.py.

voice.description: Name of the voice this profile describes, e.g. 'universal' or 'professional'.

generated.description: ISO date the profile was generated, or empty string for the shipped default.

source.description: Relative path to the source document or corpus this profile was derived from.

default_register.description: Name of the register to use when none is specified.

thresholds.description: Non-negative numeric thresholds shared across registers.

hedge_tolerance.description: Allowed distance, in hedge tokens per 100 words, from targets.hedge_per_100w_mean. Read by the checker and by references/07-verification.md.

bans.description: Named lists of banned or flagged phrases, each a list of lowercase strings.

provisional.description: Present when the corpus is under 20,000 words. Lists the rules that wait for the author's confirmation. Remove a name once the author has confirmed that rule.

rule_overrides.description: Maps a rule id to off, info, review or block for this voice.

registers.description: Named register overrides. Each register merges over DEFAULT_REGISTER; unset keys fall back to the default.

policyValue.description: Four-state policy used by semicolons, contractions, and questions.

tristateValue.description: Three-state policy used by announcement_colon, hedge_connectives, meta_commentary, tricolon, and compressed_antithesis.

tricolon.description: Default is info, which reports the hit and leaves the verdict alone.

length.description: Two-sided word band for the register. The checker blocks outside the band when min and max are both set, and reviews when only one is set.

targets.description: Numeric stylometric targets for a register. Range keys take a [low, high] pair; max keys take a single non-negative number.

rangePair.description: A [low, high] pair where low <= high.
